To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stylistic features of a writer can be characterized as the distribution of syntactic elements such as the frequency of different kinds of noun phrases and the frequency of different types of clauses.

the stylistic differences between authors are best captured by syntactic elements in the deep structure, and that the most important elements are the subject and object of a sentence, the type of verb used in a sentence, and the type of prepositional phrase.

(1) the most important syntactic features in authorship attribution are those that characterize the author's style, and that these features are not the same for all authors; (2) the most important features are the ones that are most likely to be different for different authors; (3) the most important stylistic features are not the ones that occur most frequently in the author's writing; (4) the most important style features are the ones whose probability of occurrence is different for different authors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the syntactic elements of a sentence are not as important as the semantic elements of the sentence, and that the syntactic style of a sentence is more important than the semantic style.
syntactic structure is a promising feature for authorship attribution, but the specific elements that contribute to stylistic differences vary across domains and writing styles.

syntactic elements are not only useful for stylistic analysis, but also can be used to interpret the writing styles of individual authors, and that such interpretation can be used to improve the authorship attribution performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified some stylistic elements in syntax that can help distinguish authors in different domains, but that the syntactic features are less useful in distinguishing authors in the same domain.
we have shown that the syntactic structure of a sentence can be used to characterize stylistic elements in a sentence, which in turn can help to identify the authorship of the text.
syntactic structures are a promising source of stylistic elements in writing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stylistic elements in syntactic structure are not as straightforward as we might expect, and there is no single best way to characterize stylistic elements for authorship attribution tasks.

stylistic elements in syntactic structure are more subtle than previously believed, and that a careful examination of the distributional difference in deep syntactic elements is required to understand the writing styles in syntactic structures.
syntactic elements are indeed important for authorship attribution, and that they can be interpreted in terms of rhetorical and compositional theory.
